elements.text: Manage as suspected severe malaria and refer urgently to reach referral hospital within 6 hours:

elements.section: Manage as suspected severe malaria and refer urgently to reach referral hospital within 6 hours:
elements.text: If hock2/systolic BP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 90. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.

elements.section: Manage as suspected severe malaria and refer urgently to reach referral hospital within 6 hours:
elements.text: Test for malaria with rapid test3 if available.

elements.section: Manage as suspected severe malaria and refer urgently to reach referral hospital within 6 hours:
elements.text: If positive, give artesunate 2.4mg/kg IM before referral. Indicate dose and route in referral letter.

elements.section: Manage as suspected severe malaria and refer urgently to reach referral hospital within 6 hours:
elements.text: If referral delayed, give second dose artesunate 2.4mg/kg IM 12 hours later. Notify4 within 24 hours.
MALARIA

1Check NICD: South African malaria risk map 2024: www.nicd.ac.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/National_Risk_Map-02-Dec-2025.pdf. 2If systolic BP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 3Rapid tests may stay positive for up to one month after successful treatment. A negative test does not exclude malaria, request a second test. 4 Notify via NMC App (download from NICD website/app store) or www.nicd.ac.za/nmc-overview/ notification-process. 5Known, cancer, receiving chemotherapy or long-term corticosteroids.

Suspect malaria if patient in a malaria area1 in the past 3 months and now presents with temperature ≥ 38°C, severe headache, fatigue, shivering episodes, joint/muscle pain, flu-like symptoms, dry cough, nausea and vomiting or diarrhoea.

Approach to the patient with suspected malaria not needing urgent attention Test for malaria with rapid test3, if available. If not available or rapid test negative, send blood sample to laboratory for microscopy.
• Give artemether/lumefantrine 80/480mg at 0, 8, 20, 32, 44 and 56 hours (total of 6 doses) with fatty food/milk.
- Give first dose in health facility and monitor patient for 1 hour. - If patient vomits within 1 hour of taking first dose, give metoclopramide 10mg

orally/IM. - Repeat artemether/lumefantrine 80/480mg. If patient vomits again, refer. - Explain importance of completing prescribed doses, even if patient feels better. • For pain and fever, give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for 5 days. • Advise patient to keep hydrated. • Advise to return immediately if symptoms worsen (vomiting, drowsy, confused, jaundiced) and refer urgently. • Review patient in 2 days. If no improvement in symptoms, refer.
• Give artemether/lumefantrine 80/480mg with fatty food/milk. If referral delayed, give second dose after 8 hours.
